Fast Correlation Test for a Matrix

Source: R/corTest.R
corTest.Rd

Compute correlation coefficients, p-values, and pairwise sample sizes for all variable pairs in a numeric matrix.

corTest(
  x,
  method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall"),
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  triangle = c("full", "upper", "lower"),
  maxPValue = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Numeric matrix or data.frame.

method

Character string specifying the correlation method. Passed to cor.

One of:

\"pearson\"

Pearson product-moment correlation

\"spearman\"

Spearman rank correlation

\"kendall\"

Kendall rank correlation

Default is \"pearson\".

use

Character string passed to cor. Default is \"pairwise.complete.obs\".

triangle

Character string specifying which part of the matrices should be returned.

One of:

\"full\"

Return the complete matrices

\"upper\"

Return only the upper triangle

\"lower\"

Return only the lower triangle

Default is \"full\".

maxPValue

Optional upper limit for displayed p-values. Correlations with p-values larger than maxPValue are replaced with NA.

Value

A list with three matrices:

cor

Correlation matrix

pValue

Matrix of p-values

n

Matrix of pairwise sample sizes

Details

Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlations are supported via the method argument passed to cor.

Compared to repeatedly calling cor.test, this implementation is fully vectorised and substantially faster for matrices with many variables.

Missing values are handled using pairwise complete observations.

For a Pearson correlation coefficient \(r\) with sample size \(n\), the two-sided p-value under the null hypothesis \(\rho = 0\) can be computed as:

$$ p = 2 * F_{Beta}((1 - |r|)/2, 1/2, (n-2)/2) $$

where \(F_{Beta}\) is the Beta distribution CDF.

This formulation avoids explicitly computing the t-statistic and is numerically stable for correlations close to ±1.

See also

Other test.correlation: fisherZ()

Examples

X <- matrix(rnorm(200), 50, 4)

res <- corTest(X)

# only significant correlations in the upper triangle
res2 <- corTest(
  X,
  triangle = "upper",
  maxPValue = 0.05
)
